paragraphs.text: Behold what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called children of God; and [such] we are. For this cause the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
paragraphs.original: ἴδετε ποταπὴν ἀγάπην δέδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τέκνα θεοῦ κληθῶμεν, καὶ ἐσμέν. διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κόσμος οὐ γινώσκει ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: idete potapēn agapēn dedōken hēmin ho patēr hina tekna theou klēthōmen, kai esmen. dia touto ho kosmos ou ginōskei hēmas hoti ouk egnō auton.

paragraphs.text: Beloved, now are we children of God, and it is not yet made manifest what we shall be. We know that, if he shall be manifested, we shall be like him; for we shall see him even as he is.
paragraphs.original: ἀγαπητοί, νῦν τέκνα θεοῦ ἐσμεν, καὶ οὔπω ἐφανερώθη τί ἐσόμεθα. οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐὰν φανερωθῇ ὅμοιοι αὐτῷ ἐσόμεθα, ὅτι ὀψόμεθα αὐτὸν καθώς ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: agapētoi, nyn tekna theou esmen, kai oupō ephanerōthē ti esometha. oidamen hoti ean phanerōthē homoioi autō esometha, hoti opsometha auton kathōs estin.

paragraphs.text: And every one that hath this hope [set] on him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἐλπίδα ταύτην ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἁγνίζει ἑαυτὸν καθὼς ἐκεῖνος ἁγνός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho echōn tēn elpida tautēn epʼ autō hagnizei heauton kathōs ekeinos hagnos estin.

paragraphs.text: Every one that doeth sin doeth also lawlessness; and sin is lawlessness.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιεῖ, καὶ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία.
paragraphs.translit: Pas ho poiōn tēn hamartian kai tēn anomian poiei, kai hē hamartia estin hē anomia.

paragraphs.text: And ye know that he was manifested to take away sins; and in him is no sin.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ἐφανερώθη ἵνα τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἄρῃ, καὶ ἁμαρτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai oidate hoti ekeinos ephanerōthē hina tas hamartias arē, kai hamartia en autō ouk estin.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither knoweth him.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ μένων οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτάνων οὐχ ἑώρακεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲ ἔγνωκεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: pas ho en autō menōn ouch hamartanei· pas ho hamartanōn ouch heōraken auton oude egnōken auton.

paragraphs.text: [My] little children, let no man lead you astray: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous:
paragraphs.original: τεκνία, μηδεὶς πλανάτω ὑμᾶς· ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην δίκαιός ἐστιν, καθὼς ἐκεῖνος δίκαιός ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: teknia, mēdeis planatō hymas· ho poiōn tēn dikaiosynēn dikaios estin, kathōs ekeinos dikaios estin·

paragraphs.text: he that doeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. To this end was the Son of God manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν, ὅτι ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς ὁ διάβολος ἁμαρτάνει. εἰς τοῦτο ἐφανερώθη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα λύσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου.
paragraphs.translit: ho poiōn tēn hamartian ek tou diabolou estin, hoti apʼ archēs ho diabolos hamartanei. eis touto ephanerōthē ho hyios tou theou hina lysē ta erga tou diabolou.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever is begotten of God doeth no sin, because his seed abideth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is begotten of God.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιεῖ, ὅτι σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει, καὶ οὐ δύναται ἁμαρτάνειν, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται.
paragraphs.translit: pas ho gegennēmenos ek tou theou hamartian ou poiei, hoti sperma autou en autō menei, kai ou dynatai hamartanein, hoti ek tou theou gegennētai.

paragraphs.text: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τούτῳ φανερά ἐστιν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ διαβόλου· πᾶς ὁ μὴ ποιῶν δικαιοσύνην οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: en toutō phanera estin ta tekna tou theou kai ta tekna tou diabolou· pas ho mē poiōn dikaiosynēn ouk estin ek tou theou, kai ho mē agapōn ton adelphon autou.

paragraphs.text: For this is the message which ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another:
paragraphs.original: Ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγγελία ἣν ἠκούσατε ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους·
paragraphs.translit: Hoti hautē estin hē angelia hēn ēkousate apʼ archēs, hina agapōmen allēlous·

paragraphs.text: not as Cain was of the evil one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his works were evil, and his brother`s righteous.
paragraphs.original: οὐ καθὼς Κάϊν ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἦν καὶ ἔσφαξεν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ· καὶ χάριν τίνος ἔσφαξεν αὐτόν; ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρὰ ἦν, τὰ δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ δίκαια.
paragraphs.translit: ou kathōs Kain ek tou ponērou ēn kai esphaxen ton adelphon autou· kai charin tinos esphaxen auton; hoti ta erga autou ponēra ēn, ta de tou adelphou autou dikaia.

paragraphs.text: Marvel not, brethren, if the world hateth you.
paragraphs.original: μὴ θαυμάζετε, ἀδελφοί, εἰ μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος.
paragraphs.translit: mē thaumazete, adelphoi, ei misei hymas ho kosmos.

paragraphs.text: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not abideth in death.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι μεταβεβήκαμεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν, ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τοὺς ἀδελφούς· ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν μένει ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis oidamen hoti metabebēkamen ek tou thanatou eis tēn zōēn, hoti agapōmen tous adelphous· ho mē agapōn menei en tō thanatō.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς ὁ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἐστίν, καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι πᾶς ἀνθρωποκτόνος οὐκ ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἐν αὐτῷ μένουσαν.
paragraphs.translit: pas ho misōn ton adelphon autou anthrōpoktonos estin, kai oidate hoti pas anthrōpoktonos ouk echei zōēn aiōnion en autō menousan.

paragraphs.text: Hereby know we love, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τούτῳ ἐγνώκαμεν τὴν ἀγάπην, ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν· καὶ ἡμεῖς ὀφείλομεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὰς ψυχὰς θεῖναι.
paragraphs.translit: en toutō egnōkamen tēn agapēn, hoti ekeinos hyper hēmōn tēn psychēn autou ethēken· kai hēmeis opheilomen hyper tōn adelphōn tas psychas theinai.

paragraphs.text: But whoso hath the world`s goods, and beholdeth his brother in need, and shutteth up his compassion from him, how doth the love of God abide in him?
paragraphs.original: ὃς δʼ ἂν ἔχῃ τὸν βίον τοῦ κόσμου καὶ θεωρῇ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχοντα καὶ κλείσῃ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, πῶς ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ μένει ἐν αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: hos dʼ an echē ton bion tou kosmou kai theōrē ton adelphon autou chreian echonta kai kleisē ta splanchna autou apʼ autou, pōs hē agapē tou theou menei en autō;

paragraphs.text: [My] Little children, let us not love in word, neither with the tongue; but in deed and truth.
paragraphs.original: Τεκνία, μὴ ἀγαπῶμεν λόγῳ μηδὲ τῇ γλώσσῃ ἀλλὰ ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: Teknia, mē agapōmen logō mēde tē glōssē alla en ergō kai alētheia.

paragraphs.text: Hereby shall we know that we are of the truth, and shall assure our heart before him:
paragraphs.original: ἐν τούτῳ γνωσόμεθα ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐσμέν, καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πείσομεν τὴν καρδίαν ἡμῶν
paragraphs.translit: en toutō gnōsometha hoti ek tēs alētheias esmen, kai emprosthen autou peisomen tēn kardian hēmōn

paragraphs.text: because if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐὰν καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν ἡ καρδία, ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ θεὸς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν καὶ γινώσκει πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ean kataginōskē hēmōn hē kardia, hoti meizōn estin ho theos tēs kardias hēmōn kai ginōskei panta.

paragraphs.text: Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, we have boldness toward God;
paragraphs.original: ἀγαπητοί, ἐὰν ἡ καρδία μὴ καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν, παρρησίαν ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεόν,
paragraphs.translit: agapētoi, ean hē kardia mē kataginōskē hēmōn, parrēsian echomen pros ton theon,

paragraphs.text: and whatsoever we ask we receive of him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτῶμεν λαμβάνομεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηροῦμεν καὶ τὰ ἀρεστὰ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ποιοῦμεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho ean aitōmen lambanomen apʼ autou, hoti tas entolas autou tēroumen kai ta aresta enōpion autou poioumen.

paragraphs.text: And this is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he gave us commandment.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα πιστεύσωμεν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, καθὼς ἔδωκεν ἐντολὴν ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hautē estin hē entolē autou, hina pisteusōmen tō onomati tou hyiou autou Iēsou Christou kai agapōmen allēlous, kathōs edōken entolēn hēmin.

paragraphs.text: And he that keepeth his commandments abideth in him, and he in him. And hereby we know that he abideth in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ τηρῶν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν αὐτῷ· καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι μένει ἐν ἡμῖν, ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος οὗ ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tērōn tas entolas autou en autō menei kai autos en autō· kai en toutō ginōskomen hoti menei en hēmin, ek tou pneumatos hou hēmin edōken.
